text:
A: Hi! Hello, can you hear me okay?
B: Hiya, yes, loud and clear. I'm Julie, I'm in Ossett, West Yorkshire.
A: Hi Julie, I'm Charlotte, I'm in Woking, in Surrey. Erm, I have to say, I saw your photo and I thought, oh, her office looks like mine.
B: Ha, I thought the same about yours! Grey walls, candle on the shelf. So what is it you do?
A: I'm a regional operations manager for a group of dental practices. Nine clinics across Surrey and Hampshire.
B: You're joking. I'm a regional operations manager as well. Builders' merchants, six branches across West and South Yorkshire.
A: No way! Same title! That's so funny. Sorry, I'm, erm, I didn't expect that.
B: Snap. Although I've got timber and plasterboard and you've got teeth.
A: Teeth and sterilisers, mostly. And practice managers ringing me at half seven in the morning because a nurse has called in sick.
B: Oh, staffing. That's half my life. How long have you been doing it?
A: About four years in this role. Before that I was managing a single practice. I did the CMI Level 5 through work, which sort of helped me get it, to be honest.
B: I did the CMI Level 5 as well! Company paid. I've been at mine twenty-four years, though, started on admin, so I've done the long way round.
A: Twenty-four years, that's amazing. Do you know what I mean, that's proper loyalty. Are you looking to go further, like director level?
B: Erm, that's the plan. Before I'm fifty-five. I were passed over once, a few years back, and they gave it to a lad who'd been there five minutes. So, yeah. Still a bit sore, if I'm honest.
A: Oh, that's so frustrating. I'm sort of eyeing up director as well, but quietly, you know. I don't really talk about it at work.
B: No, you don't, do you. You keep your head down, get your numbers looking right for the quarterly, and let them notice.
A: Exactly. The quarterlies stress me out so much. I lie awake the night before going through the dashboard.
B: You get used to it. It's all in how you present it, love. Same figures, different story.
A: Ha, that's very true. Is that the sort of thing, sorry, I'm talking shop. Have you got family?
B: Two, both grown up. Callum's in Leeds and Megan's at uni in Nottingham. That's them at the graduation on my shelf. And a Labrador, Bella. What about you, any kids?
A: Erm, no, not yet. Just my husband Tom and the dog. A cockapoo, Biscuit. Everyone in this study seems to have a Biscuit, Kerry's cat's called Biscuit.
B: Oh, I spoke to Kerry! Lovely girl, bit quiet. Her husband's a sparky, same as mine.
A: She was really nice. And I had Dorota as well, she's a pharmacy technician, which is what my mum does, well, sort of.
B: Small world. So what do you do of a weekend, then, when you're not doing dashboards?
A: Reformer Pilates, walking Biscuit, and Tom and I try to get to a West End show a few times a year. We saw Les Mis in the summer, I cried the whole way through.
B: I'll do a musical if there's a nice meal first. Leeds Grand, bit of steak beforehand, glass of prosecco. That's my idea of culture.
A: Oh, that's my perfect evening, honestly. Where do you go for dinner beforehand?
